args.summary: Deploy of v2.3.1 to production caused checkout-api health checks to fail across all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. Per the platform runbook, the service was rolled back to v2.3.0 — the most recent release that was healthy in production — in all regions. Post-rollback verification: service is healthy with error rate at 0.2%. The failed v2.3.1 release needs investigation before any re-deploy.
args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
All done. Here's what I did:

1. **Diagnosed the issue**: `checkout-api` v2.3.1 (deployed to all regions) was failing health checks with an 18% error rate. Deployment history showed **v2.3.0** as the most recent release that was healthy in production.
2. **Rolled back**: Deployed v2.3.0 to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west).
3. **Verified recovery**: The service is now healthy with the error rate down to 0.2%.
4. **Opened incident**: Created a SEV2 incident (**INC-0001**) documenting the failed v2.3.1 deploy, the rollback to v2.3.0, and the post-rollback verification. On-call has been paged.

Note: v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production, so any attempt to re-deploy it will require change-manager approval per organizational policy.
